annotations.label: Converse L'Hôpital Fails
annotations.description: The main counterexample: f(x) = x + sin(x), g(x) = x gives lim f/g = 1 (ratio converges) but lim f'/g' = lim(1 + cos x) does not exist. Fully verified, 0 sorries.
annotations.mathContent: lhopital_converse_fails : (Tendsto (fun x => (x + sin x) / x) atTop (𝓝 1)) ∧ (¬∃ L, Tendsto (fun x => (1 + cos x) / 1) atTop (𝓝 L))

annotations.label: sin(x)/x → 0
annotations.description: The key helper lemma: sin(x)/x → 0 as x → ∞. Proved by direct ε-N using |sin x| ≤ 1 to bound |sin x / x| ≤ 1/x, then choosing N = 1/ε + 1.
annotations.mathContent: tendsto_sin_div_atTop : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => sin x / x) atTop (𝓝 0)

annotations.label: Ratio Converges to 1
annotations.description: The ratio (x + sin x)/x → 1 as x → ∞, proved by rewriting as 1 + sin(x)/x → 1 + 0 = 1.
annotations.mathContent: lim_ratio_eq_one : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (x + sin x) / x) atTop (𝓝 1)

annotations.label: Derivative Ratio Has No Limit
annotations.description: The function 1 + cos x has no limit as x → ∞. Uses cos(n*2π) = 1 and cos(n*2π+π) = -1 to find subsequential limits 2 and 0, which contradicts limit uniqueness.
annotations.mathContent: deriv_ratio_no_limit : ¬∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => 1 + cos x) atTop (𝓝 L)
